question: Does a synthetic gradient-avalanche probe reveal a finite-size exponent D that crosses the extensive boundary D = 1 at grokking, and can that crossing serve as a task-agnostic early warning?

key_findings.claim: The TDU-OFC probe converts each minibatch gradient into a synthetic avalanche on a fixed random graph over parameters rather than measuring cascades on the network's computational graph.
key_findings.evidence: The method selects the top 10% of parameters by absolute gradient, connects parameters with a Barabasi-Albert graph of attachment m = 2, redistributes active gradient mass to graph neighbors with alpha = 0.3, and stops after at most 20 iterations.

key_findings.claim: The headline trajectories are not cleanly established as outputs of a purely offline, observational probe.
key_findings.evidence: The abstract and introduction call TDU-OFC offline, yet the Methods introduce a separate shadow condition with alpha_train = 0 in which parameters update with raw gradients while avalanches are computed from copies. Figure 6 reports that the probe-on condition rotates XOR gradients by about 30.6 degrees and differs from shadow D by as much as 0.14 for ModAdd and 0.11 for XOR. This protocol implies that probe-on training uses transformed gradients; only the shadow trajectory is unambiguously observational, so matching the full headline crossing under shadow training is necessary before calling the main result offline or non-invasive.

key_findings.claim: Dimensional criticality is operationally defined as the exponent D in s_max proportional to N^D crossing one across a population of model sizes.
key_findings.evidence: At each relative time, the largest avalanche statistic is regressed against parameter count N; D greater than one is labeled superextensive, D less than one subextensive, and D = 1 the critical boundary.

key_findings.claim: For modular addition modulo 59, the paper reports D_pre = 1.12 +/- 0.02 and D_post = 0.92 +/- 0.02, with the fitted curve crossing D = 1 near the accuracy transition.
key_findings.evidence: The time-resolved curve in Figure 2 aligns each run by g, defined as the first sampled epoch with test accuracy above 0.99. Figure 4 then reports a strict pre/post split using 5,000 bootstrap resamples of seed-epoch observations and the stated D estimates.

key_findings.claim: The stronger assertion that D crosses one precisely at t = 0 is inconsistent with the paper's own event-time estimates and plotted curves.
key_findings.evidence: For both modular primes the paper reports D_0 = 0.89 +/- 0.03 and 0.91 +/- 0.03 at the grokking epoch, already below one; the rendered Figure 2 places the ModAdd crossing before t = 0 and labels only a broad critical window |t| <= 0.5. The supported claim is a transition-localized crossing near grokking, not equality to D = 1 precisely at the behavioral event. XOR likewise approaches the boundary from below around t = 0 rather than supplying a numerically demonstrated equality at the event.

key_findings.claim: The core D curve is necessarily retrospective and cross-sectional, not an observable available from one training run before it groks.
key_findings.evidence: Relative time t = (epoch - g)/g requires the future grokking epoch g, and estimating D at any t requires a regression across widths. Runs that do not grok have no g and cannot enter the aligned analysis.

anchors.section: II.d-e Temporal aggregation and grokking-aligned FSS

key_findings.claim: The claimed 100-200 epoch early warning is not evaluated as a prospective prediction problem.
key_findings.evidence: The manuscript infers lead time from the retrospectively aligned average D curve and supplies no frozen threshold, held-out widths or seeds, sensitivity, specificity, false-alarm rate, or comparison against elapsed time and ordinary training metrics.

anchors.section: III.C Negative controls and modulus robustness

key_findings.claim: The primary size-scaling result uses only six canonical Transformer sizes, so leverage and finite-size sensitivity remain substantial.
key_findings.evidence: The canonical FSS support is d_model = 24-128 with parameter counts 6,635, 10,363, 20,123, 32,955, 67,835, and 115,003. The separately stated g in [29, 3,000] range covers the broader d_model = 16-128 sweep and therefore should not be attributed specifically to all six canonical widths. Leaving out an extreme canonical size shifts fitted D by as much as about 0.08.

anchors.section: III.C Negative controls and modulus robustness

key_findings.claim: The absolute-time grokked-versus-ungrokked control changes the very width support from which D is computed.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 5 compares 35 grokked runs drawn only from the six canonical widths with 12 ungrokked runs drawn from all available widths. Because D is a slope across N, unequal size populations and run counts directly confound the claimed trajectory difference.

anchors.section: III.C Negative controls and modulus robustness

key_findings.claim: The finite-size collapse and cutoff exponent are not independent confirmations of the crossing.
key_findings.evidence: The epoch statistic sums avalanche sizes over batches, the scaling distribution pools epochs within +/-500 of the already known transition, and the 95th-percentile cutoff is fit over the same six sizes, producing D_cut about 1.02 with R-squared near one.

key_findings.claim: The only reported alpha/threshold sweep does not establish robustness of D itself and is confined to XOR.
key_findings.evidence: The 36-run sweep combines alpha in {0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5}, thresholds at the 85th, 90th, and 95th percentiles, and three seeds per configuration, but reports only that grokking timing changes by less than 3% with p > 0.7. It does not report D estimates, crossing location, shadow discrepancy, or finite-size slopes across those settings, and it does not repeat the sweep for the headline ModAdd experiment.

key_findings.claim: A Gaussian-gradient control also yields D approximately one, suggesting that extensivity is a construction baseline rather than specific evidence of learned criticality.
key_findings.evidence: The top-10% threshold activates a number of components proportional to N and propagation is capped at 20 rounds; synthetic Gaussian gradients give D near one under the same machinery.

anchors.section: II.b TDU-OFC avalanche probe / Gaussian control

key_findings.claim: The probe is not shown to recover a conventional avalanche universality class.
key_findings.evidence: Heavy tails are displayed through complementary cumulative curves, but the paper does not estimate a tail exponent with likelihood methods, test goodness of fit, compare lognormal or exponential alternatives, or verify crackling-noise exponent relations.

key_findings.claim: The XOR experiment reverses the direction of the D transition and does not test delayed train-to-test generalization.
key_findings.evidence: The two-layer MLP is evaluated on all four XOR examples with no held-out test split and defines its event when accuracy exceeds 0.99; D moves in the opposite direction from modular addition.

key_findings.claim: The XOR result cannot support a task-agnostic grokking attractor because it is ordinary four-example fitting under a redefined transition criterion.
key_findings.evidence: With no train-test separation, the central delayed-generalization property of grokking is absent; two task-architecture pairs with opposite exponent directions do not establish a shared universal mechanism.

key_findings.claim: The shadow alpha = 0 comparison shows that the artificial redistribution can be comparable to the reported pre/post effect size.
key_findings.evidence: The maximum difference between probe-on and shadow curves is about 0.14 for modular addition and 0.11 for XOR, while the modular-addition pre/post separation is only about 0.20; describing this perturbation as negligible is therefore not scale-free.

key_findings.claim: The analysis does not causally connect D to grokking outcome or timing.
key_findings.evidence: No intervention selectively increases or decreases the fitted exponent and then measures generalization. The shadow comparison changes the measurement propagation coefficient, not the underlying trained model's critical state under a matched outcome experiment.

key_findings.claim: Seed, compute, and data reporting is insufficient for a fully matched finite-size estimate.
key_findings.evidence: The paper gives 80/20 splits of all 3,481 modulo-59 pairs and optimizer hyperparameters, but the per-width seed counts, complete run budgets, checkpoint frequency, failed-run handling, and independence structure behind seed-epoch bootstrap resampling are not fully specified.

key_findings.claim: The paper's phase-transition evidence is finite-size scaling of an artificial observable, not a demonstrated thermodynamic nonanalyticity.
key_findings.evidence: The order criterion is D = 1 and accuracy crossing 0.99. Although multiple widths are used, no control parameter limit, susceptibility divergence, critical exponent relation, or genuine model-size collapse independent of the random probe is established.

method.core_idea: Map minibatch gradients to synthetic avalanches, infer a cross-width extensivity exponent, and align that exponent around each run's future grokking epoch; a separate alpha_train = 0 shadow mode computes avalanches from copied raw gradients.
method.mechanism: A fixed top-fraction threshold and random scale-free parameter graph create cascades by redistributing gradient mass. Maximum or aggregated avalanche sizes are fit against total parameter count; crossing D = 1 is interpreted as a change between superextensive and subextensive gradient coordination. The probe-on/shadow distinction matters because the former rotates update gradients while only the latter is demonstrably offline.
assumptions: A Barabasi-Albert graph over parameter indices is a meaningful substrate for gradient coordination despite ignoring architecture and tensor structure.
The top-10% threshold and 20-step cap do not mechanically impose extensive scaling.
Six widths and their heterogeneous grokking epochs form an adequate finite-size ensemble.
Bootstrap seed-epoch observations provide valid uncertainty despite temporal and within-seed dependence.
An exponent fitted across widths can be converted into an actionable early warning for an individual run.
Probe-on and alpha_train = 0 shadow training are sufficiently equivalent even though the reported maximum D discrepancy is 0.14 and the probe rotates XOR gradients by about 30.6 degrees.
Robust grokking timing in the XOR alpha/threshold sweep implies robustness of the D exponent even though D sensitivity is not reported.

techniques.role: Transforms batch gradients into cascades on a fixed Barabasi-Albert parameter graph.
Fits avalanche maxima and cutoffs against parameter count to estimate D.
Normalizes epochs by the future grokking time before pooling trajectories.
Compares alpha = 0 propagation and synthetic Gaussian gradients with the main probe.

evaluations.setting: Modulo-59 addition with six Transformer sizes
evaluations.metric: Cross-width exponent D before and after test accuracy exceeds 0.99
evaluations.result: D falls from 1.12 +/- 0.02 to 0.92 +/- 0.02 on retrospectively aligned trajectories.
D_cut is about 1.02 with R-squared near one over six sizes, using the same transition-selected data window.
evaluations.baseline: Gaussian-gradient control with D approximately one

evaluations.result: Modulo-47 gives D around 0.91 +/- 0.03 versus 0.89 +/- 0.03 for modulo 59; XOR shows a transition in the opposite direction without a train-test split.

evaluations.setting: Absolute-time grokked versus ungrokked modular-addition runs
evaluations.result: Thirty-five grokked and twelve ungrokked runs appear different, but the groups use different width supports and D is itself a width-regression slope.
evaluations.baseline: Ungrokked runs from a broader set of widths

evaluations.setting: Claimed absolute-time early warning in ModAdd-59 (discussion and Figure 5)
evaluations.metric: Cross-sectional D at epoch 100 and lead time before behavioral grokking
evaluations.result: The paper gives an illustrative separation of D about 1.02 versus 1.75 at epoch 100 with R-squared at least 0.95 and claims a 100-200 epoch lead, but supplies no held-out classifier, threshold, false-alarm rate, or width-matched support.
evaluations.baseline: Ungrokked population with different width support; no elapsed-time, loss, or single-run forecasting baseline

evaluations.setting: Probe-on versus alpha_train = 0 shadow control in the critical window
evaluations.metric: Gradient angular deviation and maximum absolute D difference
evaluations.result: The probe-on XOR update rotates gradients by about 30.6 degrees (mean cosine about 0.86); max |D_shadow - D_on| is at most 0.14 for ModAdd and 0.11 for XOR.
evaluations.baseline: Raw-gradient shadow training, the only condition explicitly described as computing avalanches offline from copied gradients

limitations: Author-stated: only modular addition and XOR are examined, and broader task/architecture evidence is needed.
Author-stated: finite model sizes and dependence on probe hyperparameters limit universality claims.
Reviewer inference: relative-time alignment leaks the future transition and excludes non-grokkers.
Reviewer inference: the grokked/ungrokked control is width- and count-mismatched, which directly confounds a scaling exponent.
Reviewer inference: six sizes, extreme-point sensitivity, and correlated bootstrap units understate finite-size uncertainty.
Reviewer inference: heavy-tail and data-collapse plots lack distributional model comparison and independent validation.
Reviewer inference: data and implementation are available only on request, and seed-level protocol details are incomplete.
Contradiction audit: D at t = 0 is reported as 0.89 +/- 0.03 (ModAdd-59) and 0.91 +/- 0.03 (ModAdd-47), so the evidence supports a crossing near the event rather than precisely at D = 1 and t = 0.
Contradiction audit: only the alpha_train = 0 shadow path is explicitly offline; probe-on training rotates gradients and can move D by 0.11-0.14 relative to shadow.
Reviewer inference: the 36-run alpha/threshold sweep is XOR-only and reports grokking time, not exponent or crossing robustness.
failure_modes: Top-fraction thresholding can force active mass to scale with N and make D near one a probe artifact.
Changing the random graph realization or attachment rule can change cascade geometry independently of the trained model.
A maximum statistic can be dominated by outliers, batch count, or training-window length.
Relative-time alignment can manufacture an apparently sharp population crossing from heterogeneous smooth trajectories.
A D estimate cannot be formed for a single width without an auxiliary size ensemble.
Runs that never grok within budget can be silently omitted from the aligned signal.
XOR-style fitting transitions can be mistaken for delayed generalization when the operational definition is broadened.
Training with probe-transformed rather than raw gradients can create or shift the trajectory being presented as an offline diagnostic.
Pooling a fixed +/-500 absolute-epoch window around transitions as early as tens of epochs yields highly unequal relative-time and pre/post support across widths.
reusable_insights: Any finite-size early warning should be evaluated prospectively on held-out size ensembles and also translated into a single-run decision rule.
Controls for a scaling exponent must match the support and weighting of system sizes exactly.
Avalanche claims require fitted tail alternatives, likelihood-based goodness of fit, and exponent-relation tests beyond visual CCDFs.
Synthetic measurement graphs should be compared with architecture-aware connectivity and multiple graph nulls.
Transition alignment is useful descriptively but should never be the sole evidence for prediction.
open_questions: Can a past-only D estimator predict held-out grokking events without knowing g and without pooling the test run with other widths?
Does the claimed crossing survive exact width-matched grokked and censored controls with hierarchical seed-level uncertainty?
How sensitive are D and lead time to threshold percentile, graph family, graph seed, propagation coefficient, and iteration cap?
Do architecture-aware parameter graphs yield the same exponent and task-direction reversal?
Can an intervention that changes avalanche coordination while matching loss and update norm causally change grokking probability or time?

competitive_landscape.title: Early-Warning Signals of Grokking via Loss-Landscape Geometry
competitive_landscape.relationship: closest prior direct grokking early-warning and causal-mechanism competitor
competitive_landscape.difference: Xu's v3 predates the reviewed paper and reports a commutator-defect precursor across modular arithmetic, SCAN, and Dyck-1, including interventions that accelerate grokking by roughly 32% on SCAN and 50% on Dyck or delay/prevent it by suppressing orthogonal flow. The reviewed D statistic is a retrospective cross-width synthetic-graph fit with no prospective held-out prediction or D intervention, so broad priority for an architecture-agnostic early warning is not supported.

competitive_landscape.title: From Density Matrices to Phase Transitions in Deep Learning: Spectral Early Warnings and Interpretability
competitive_landscape.relationship: prior direct spectral early-warning and dimensionality competitor
competitive_landscape.difference: Hennick and Corlouer derive spectral heat capacity as an early warning under critical slowing down and participation ratio as reorganization dimensionality, then evaluate four settings including grokking. The reviewed work instead uses a random parameter graph and event-aligned finite-size exponent, without a comparable past-only forecasting test or theorem.

competitive_landscape.title: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability
competitive_landscape.difference: Nanda et al. recover the modular-addition Fourier circuit, validate it with ablations, and expose gradual circuit formation and cleanup on individual trajectories. D is task-agnostic in construction but requires a population of widths and does not reveal the computation that generalizes or yield a validated single-run decision rule.

competitive_landscape.title: Information-Theoretic Progress Measures reveal Grokking is an Emergent Phase Transition
competitive_landscape.difference: Clauw et al. track higher-order neuronal synergy and redundancy, identify phases before grokking, and state that these measures anticipate the event. The reviewed paper introduces a different gradient-cascade observable but does not compare forecasting performance against that representation-based signal.

competitive_landscape.title: Toward a Physics of Deep Learning and Brains
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct avalanche, susceptibility, and finite-size-scaling predecessor
competitive_landscape.difference: Ghavasieh et al. already apply neuronal-avalanche equations, susceptibility, crackling relations, and finite-size scaling to deep networks, identify universality classes, and explicitly characterize the driven regime as quasi-critical. The reviewed paper adds grokking-aligned gradient cascades but lacks comparable tail-model and exponent-relation validation.

competitive_landscape.title: Tuning Universality in Deep Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Ghavasieh derives stochastic information-propagation couplings, a Landau description, and distinct avalanche universality classes with activation-controlled simulations. The reviewed paper fits one exponent on a random parameter graph and explicitly leaves its universality class open.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking as a First Order Phase Transition in Two Layer Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Rubin et al. analytically map feature-learning grokking in tractable two-layer teacher-student models to a first-order mixed phase and test the associated representations. The reviewed work labels a fitted D = 1 crossover an order parameter but supplies no free-energy competition, nonanalytic limit, or theorem connecting D to generalization.

competitive_landscape.title: Is Grokking a Computational Glass Relaxation?
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct landscape mechanism and thermodynamic-claim competitor
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang et al. sample an entropy landscape, report no entropy barrier in their grokking transition, and construct optimizer counterexamples to simple norm-based accounts. D is correlational and is not tested for discriminating a glass relaxation, first-order transition, gradual circuit formation, or probe-induced scaling.

competitive_landscape.title: Noise-Driven Escape from Metastable Phases explains Grokking in Deep Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Ersoy and Wiesner deliberately trap deep linear networks, vary SGD noise, and report Arrhenius escape behavior over two orders of magnitude in time. This later work supplies an intervention-based metastability account; the reviewed paper's D crossing remains a non-causal diagnostic and is not compared against basin/noise variables.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a universal dimensional transition at grokking: gradient avalanches switch across D = 1, yielding a task-agnostic early warning and a critical attractor shared by Transformers and MLPs.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Six canonical modulo-59 widths give a retrospectively aligned D_pre = 1.12 +/- 0.02 versus D_post = 0.92 +/- 0.02; modulo 47 gives D_0 = 0.91 +/- 0.03 versus 0.89 +/- 0.03 for modulo 59, and XOR supplies an opposite-direction curve. However, both modular D_0 values are below one rather than equal to one at t = 0, the Gaussian construction itself yields D about one, the probe-on/shadow discrepancy reaches 0.14, and the early-warning comparison is neither width-matched nor prospectively evaluated.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the specific TDU-OFC synthetic gradient-cascade construction combined with grokking-aligned, cross-width D estimation. The independently searched primary literature already contains neural avalanches and finite-size scaling (arXiv:2509.22649v1; 2512.00168v1), mechanistic and information-theoretic grokking progress measures (2301.05217v3; 2408.08944v1), analytic and landscape phase-transition accounts (2310.03789v3; 2505.11411v5), and—most importantly—an earlier direct architecture-agnostic, intervention-tested grokking warning based on commutator defect (2602.16967v3) plus a prior spectral early-warning framework (2603.29805v2). The reviewed combination of a random parameter graph, an extensivity exponent, and event alignment was not found in those records, but priority for a task-agnostic early warning, a universal critical attractor, or a causal mechanism is not supported. The signal uses future g, XOR lacks held-out generalization, the control populations are width-mismatched, and only shadow training is demonstrably offline.

reviewer_notes: Secondary verification re-read all nine pages of the exact arXiv:2604.16431v1 artifact end to end, including equations and Methods on pages 2-3, every plotted and captioned result on pages 4-6, discussion/limitations/data availability on pages 6-8, and all references on pages 8-9; this revision contains no appendix or supplement. Rendered pages 2, 4, 5, and 6 were visually inspected to resolve the probe protocol, crossing location, bootstrap/control figures, and exact captions. The official record identifies v1 as submitted 2026-04-06 (the PDF is dated 2026-04-21). The repository PDF SHA-256 was rechecked as f0947f5fdcd4f476caa5429f8228d9213805b17d47e6d8e64859387a23eaee85, matching the index; the indexed unversioned export locator, text hash, page count, and extraction timestamp are preserved exactly. Concrete repairs distinguish a near-event crossing from the abstract's precise-at-t=0 claim, the broader d_model = 16-128 timing range from the six d_model = 24-128 canonical widths, and the truly offline shadow condition from probe-on training. Four independent search families—grokking early warnings/progress measures, neural avalanches/finite-size scaling, spectral/thermodynamic criticality, and causal/metastable mechanisms—were checked against current official primary records. Confidence remains below certainty because run-level data, code, per-width seed accounting, and fully matched raw-gradient trajectories are unavailable.

Rendered pages 2, 4, 5, and 6 were checked visually. Every finding and page anchor was rechecked, including D_pre = 1.12 +/- 0.02, D_post = 0.92 +/- 0.02, D_0 = 0.89/0.91, D_cut about 1.02, six canonical parameter counts, 5,000 bootstrap resamples, the 35-versus-12 control, the 36-run XOR sensitivity sweep, 30.6-degree gradient rotation, and 0.14/0.11 shadow discrepancies.
verification.competitor_check: Re-searched official current primary literature on 2026-08-23 using four query families: grokking early-warning/progress measures, neural avalanche finite-size scaling, spectral/thermodynamic phase signals, and causal/metastable grokking mechanisms. Opened and version-checked arXiv:2602.16967v3 (2026-04-03), 2603.29805v2 (2026-04-01), 2301.05217v3 (2023-10-19), 2408.08944v1 (2024-08-16), 2509.22649v1 (2025-09-26), 2512.00168v1 (2025-11-28), 2310.03789v3 (2024-05-05), 2505.11411v5 (2026-01-03), and 2606.17120v1 (2026-06-15). The direct prior 2602.16967v3 already combines a task-spanning early-warning signal with causal interventions, narrowing the reviewed paper's broad priority claim; none of the checked records was found to contain the exact TDU-OFC random-gradient-graph plus event-aligned cross-width D construction.
